built_on: IAM Lab 5 directory (labs/lab5-ad-to-cloud-idp): same forest, OUs, groups, and accounts
exercise_source: Department-transfer (mover) exercise posted by Cyber and Chill (@cyberandchill), Nov 6, 2026: create two departments with different access, move an employee from one to the other, work out what they should lose and what they should gain.

keep_identity: Same account (mdoyle) and SID: a move never deletes and recreates the account
Email address and MFA enrollment carry over: identity persists, entitlements change
Account stays enabled: a mover is not a leaver

GG_Salesforce_Users.note: Per-person pilot group from Lab 5. The mover is not a member; listed so the model covers every group the validator knows.

GG_VPN_Access.note: Per-person grant. Lab 5 directory rule: granted per person, removed on role change. A mover does not carry VPN automatically; the new role must re-justify it.

policy_notes: Remove before you add, in the same change window: the account must never hold both departments' access at once.
Department groups are never carried across a move. Per-person groups (VPN, app pilots) are removed and re-justified by the new role, never silently kept.

The add-only move (new group added, old groups forgotten) is the classic mover failure: it leaves privilege accumulation and a segregation-of-duties conflict, here billing workqueue access held at the same time as a clinical viewer role.
